candidates.title: Parallel Octobers
candidates.pitch: The visitor chooses a team with a dated early-season record, such as a winless start, and the page replays its season thousands of times in parallel from the same talent, drawing every path as a branching, root-like fan across the 84-game calendar. Before each reveal the visitor sets a compass needle to forecast the final points; the engine then shows how much of the start was luck on a gauge, and discarding the first games from the sample shows the estimate move.
candidates.whyNow: Two ugly starts are the talk of the league on 2026-10-12 (a team still without a point and a franchise-record losing run), and 2026-27 is the first 84-game season since 1993-94, so the old 82-game rules of thumb for how deep a hole is no longer apply.

research.summary: As of 2026-10-12 the NHL season is under two weeks old and the storylines are extreme starts: reported results have the Calgary club still pointless after a 4-2 loss on 2026-10-11 and the Philadelphia club at a franchise-record seven straight losses to open the year, while others (Winnipeg, Edmonton, New York Rangers) started hot in snapshots around 2026-10-09. The league moved to an 84-game schedule this season (1,344 games, 42 home and 42 road per team), which changes the arithmetic of how recoverable a bad start is. PDO (on-ice shooting % plus save %) is the standard luck proxy and regresses toward 100 over large samples. Standings snapshots from different sites disagree by game count, so the page must carry its own snapshot date and label each record with its source and date; unconfirmed records are shown as reported.

facts.claim: The 2026-27 NHL regular season is 84 games per team (1,344 games in all, 42 home and 42 road for each club), the first 84-game season since 1993-94.
PDO is on-ice shooting percentage plus on-ice save percentage; it is treated as a luck proxy that regresses toward the league level over large samples.
As of 2026-10-11, per Canadian Press via PA Now, the Calgary Flames were still without a point after a 4-2 loss to Anaheim; reported, not confirmed by a second outlet.
As of 2026-10-12, per an AP wire report, Philadelphia had lost its first seven games of 2026-27, a franchise record, outscored 28-8; a single wire story, unconfirmed by an independent outlet.
Standings pages disagree on game counts for the same days (a snapshot around 2026-10-09 put Calgary at 0-4-0 with a -17 goal differential), so records must be shown with their own as-of date.

inspirations: fan charts in election and weather forecasting

design.coreLoop: Each round presents a team and its dated start. The visitor drags a compass needle (direction = expect a recovery or a slump, length = confidence) to forecast final points, optionally discards early games to test how fragile the read is, then commits. A web worker runs 2,000 seeded season paths from a posterior over team talent; paths are drawn as a branching fan, the forecast is scored with a proper scoring rule, and a luck gauge says how much of the start was PDO noise. Streaks and a calibration chart reward the tenth round because the visitor learns to trust fewer games less.
sophisticationHooks: Grid posterior over team talent: a prior from a hand-set tier rating times a likelihood from the dated early record, so a 0-7 start moves the estimate far less than intuition says
Seeded Poisson goal model with overtime and shootout logic and the loser point, run in a worker for 2,000 paths of 84 games, with a simulated field for the playoff line
Proper scoring (log or CRPS-style) with a calibration curve over the visitor's rounds, plus the discard-games slider showing how the estimate shifts
Branching fan chart on canvas where path density forms a mycelium-like network and a compass dial doubles as the input
design.scopeForOneDay: Build the talent posterior, season-path engine, worker, fan chart, compass input, scoring and share hash. Bundle a small dated snapshot (8 to 12 teams with record, as-of date and source; unconfirmed records labelled reported) plus a seeded generator for fictional teams so play continues beyond the real snapshot. Cut live data, full 32-team playoff simulation and player-level stats; the other 31 clubs are a simulated field and labelled as simulation.
risks: Early records come from search digests that disagree: the page shows each as of its date and source, and marks the Calgary and Philadelphia records as reported, per the cited outlet, until a verifier confirms them
Talent priors are hand-set estimates, not data: label them as estimates and keep fictional teams available so no real-team claim depends on them
Could read as a simulator: keep the forecasting game and scoring central, not a free-form sandbox
News-bound start records go stale after a few days: the snapshot is dated and fictional-team mode keeps the page useful

candidates.title: Sin Bin Concierge
candidates.pitch: You run the penalty box as a tiny, deadpan hotel: guests arrive with minors, double minors, majors and misconducts, goals go in, whistles blow, and you must announce who checks out and what the strength on the ice is, before the clock runs out. A real rules engine decides the right answer, including the awkward cases like coincidental minors, a goal on a stacked kill, and a major that refuses to leave early.
candidates.whyNow: Timeless, but the 2026-27 season is only two weeks old, penalty-heavy early games are in the news, and a faithful penalty-clock puzzle is the kind of rule detail fans argue about; it is a humor entry that rewards learning real rules.

research.summary: Hockey penalty expiry is a small state machine with surprising edge cases. A minor ends early when the power-play team scores; a major runs its full five minutes regardless; a double minor is two consecutive two-minute blocks, and a goal cancels only the block currently running; coincidental minors in the NHL produce four-on-four play and a goal does not release them. Sources found are general explainers and an older rulebook excerpt, so the spec phase must confirm wording against the current official NHL rulebook, and unconfirmed rules are shown as a simplified house version. The 2026-27 season has few penalty-rule changes (a new neck-protection requirement and an 84-game schedule were reported), so the engine does not depend on news.

Reported rule: a major penalty runs its full five minutes even if the opponent scores, while a minor ends on a power-play goal; one search digest blended several explainers, so this is shown as a simplified house rule until checked against the official rulebook.

Reported rule: in the NHL, coincidental minors at even strength produce four-on-four play, unlike USA Hockey and IIHF rules, per a Wikipedia article summary; unconfirmed until read against the current NHL rulebook.
Reported rule: a power-play goal during a double minor cancels only the two-minute block being served, per a Wikipedia article summary; unconfirmed against the NHL rulebook.

design.coreLoop: A seeded game script produces a timeline of whistles, goals and expiries. At each decision point the concierge sees the box ledger (guest, penalty, clock) and must tap who is released and set the on-ice strength, before a patience meter runs out. The rules engine scores each answer, explains the ruling in one deadpan line, and ramps difficulty by stacking penalties, adding coincidentals, majors, misconducts and goals mid-kill. Shifts are daily-seeded and shareable via URL hash so friends compare rulings.
sophisticationHooks: Pure, tested penalty-clock state machine: queue ordering of simultaneous penalties, double minor block logic, major versus minor release on goals, coincidental handling, minimum skater counts
Scenario generator with seeded randomness that guarantees each shift contains specific edge cases at rising difficulty and never an ambiguous ruling
Explanations built from the same rule trace the engine used, so every correct and wrong answer is teachable
Absurd framing: invented guests and teams, a hotel-ledger look drawn in SVG and CSS, keyboard-only play and a replay of the ruling
design.scopeForOneDay: Build the rules engine with tests, scenario generator, ledger and rink-strength UI, scoring, daily seed and share hash, about panel listing the simplified rules. Cut referee signals, audio, per-league rule variants and delayed penalties, which are listed as house rules.
risks: Rule wording comes from search digests and an older rulebook excerpt: the spec must state the exact rules implemented, label them a simplified house version and avoid calling them official until verified
Ambiguity in edge cases such as stacked coincidentals could produce a wrong answer: restrict the generator to cases the engine and a verifier agree on
Humor could feel thin once the rules click: vary the guest personas and add a late-night mode with chained events
Must use invented players and teams only; no real names, logos or marks
